title: Variant Inspector — Intervention Playbook and UX notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the UX notes, on-screen wiring, and an operator intervention playbook for a new console feature: Variant Inspector. It is intended to help operators run short-lived canaries, A/B experiments, and handle automatic or manual fallbacks with clear, auditable actions. This is a working draft — goal is to land a wireframe and grooming backlog before sprint planning.

Problem framing / why this exists:
- Current rollout UI focuses on high-level traffic split and health checks but lacks a fast operator surface to investigate per-variant behaviour (latency tails, error modes, hallucination rate, quality regressions).
- During noisy canaries operators are forced to jump between charts, logs, and raw traces; decision to rollback/fallback lacks a clear single-click path and audit trail.
- We need a console flow that surfaces signals, recommends actions, and captures operator intent for audits.

Goals for Variant Inspector feature:
1) Show per-variant telemetry (p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, error rate, quality score delta vs baseline) in one compact card.
2) Provide contextual recommended actions (pause, mute, scale-down, reroute, immediate fallback to baseline) with safety confirmations and a brief rationale.
3) Support quick A/B comparisons with side-by-side examples of model outputs for sampled queries.
4) Create a mandatory short comment and tag when an operator executes an intervention for traceability.
5) Allow scheduled auto-fallback policies to be tuned from the same panel.

Key screens / wireframe writeups (textual descriptions):
1) Variant Summary Row (list view)
   - Location: rollout detail > top of page, horizontal strip per variant.
   - Elements: variant name + label (canary, blue, green), current traffic %, small sparkline for latency, error badge (red/orange/grey), quality delta pill (+/- %), last-sampled-output quick peek ("Show example").
   - Interaction: click row opens Variant Inspector modal (deep-dive).

2) Variant Inspector Modal (primary operator surface)
   - Header: variant name, active traffic, buttons: "Pause variant", "Mute alerts", "Trigger immediate fallback" (primary danger), "Create issue".
   - Left column: Key metrics cards (latency histogram, token cost trend, error breakdown by code, throughput). Each card has a 3-state indicator (OK / Degraded / Critical) and an inline tooltip explaining thresholds.
   - Middle column: Quality panel with A/B compare tool: shows 3 sampled user requests with outputs from baseline vs this variant. Operator can toggle to see more samples and mark sample as "problematic".
   - Right column: Decision panel with recommended actions derived from rule engine. Each recommendation includes: reason (e.g., p99 > 2s and hallucination-rate +6%), impact estimate (approx. tokens saved, latency change), and confidence score.
   - Bottom: Action bar with primary Confirm button and required brief comment input. Actions are: "Pause traffic to variant", "Reduce traffic to X%", "Scale variant down (instances)", "Fallback to baseline model", "Force-rollback to last known-good".
   - Safety: If operator chooses fallback/rollback, show a short verification modal listing dependent routes and estimated disruption + checkbox list to acknowledge. Auto-populate audit comment with suggested template but allow edits.

3) Timeline / Audit Trail (expanded view)
   - Timeline shows chronological actions, auto-policy triggers, and metric snapshots at time of action. Each item includes who acted, action type, short comment, and link to related ticket.

4) Policy Tuner (inline)
   - Compact interface to tweak auto-fallback rules: metric selector (p99, error-rate, hallucination-rate), threshold, evaluation window, action (percent traffic shift, fallback). Add a "dry run" toggle to preview which segments would have been affected historically.

Microcopy and copy principles (short list):
- Use active, accountable verbs: "Pause variant" not "Disable variant".
- For risky actions include short rationale line: "Fallback will route requests to Variant A (baseline) until operator re-enables this variant."
- Consent + audit: "You must add a 1–3 sentence note describing why you intervened (for audit)."
- Toasts: "Variant paused — traffic routed to baseline. Undo" (include 30s undo).
- Error states: "Could not apply action — check workspace permissions, retry, or contact SRE."

Operator intervention playbook (step-by-step):
- Detection: Variant Inspector recommended fallback due to: sustained p99 > 2s for 5 minutes or quality regression > 5% on evaluation dataset.
- Quick triage (<= 2 min): open inspector -> review p99 and error breakdown -> sample 3 recent outputs -> check recent deploy events -> if clear quality regression, select "Fallback to baseline".
- If ambiguous, reduce traffic to 10% and enable "QA hold" (no further automatic ramp) + create issue in tracker.
- Post-action: operator must add comment + select tags (incident, false-positive, model-bug). System auto-schedules a short postmortem prompt for the rollout owner.

Backlog grooming items (these should become tickets):
- [JIRA-9251] Variant Inspector modal: metric cards + 3-state indicator (frontend + metrics API).
- [JIRA-9252] Sample compare: store and surface K sample request/response pairs with redaction.
- [JIRA-9253] Action audit trail: persistent timeline store and UI.
- [JIRA-9254] Policy tuner: add dry-run evaluation and historical preview.
- [JIRA-9255] Microcopy pass and accessible confirmation flows (a11y keyboard + screenreader).
- [JIRA-9256] Undo window implementation for risky actions (30s toast + endpoint to revert).
- [JIRA-9257] RBAC check: only variant-operators and release-managers can execute fallback; others see recommendations.

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve in grooming: 
- Visibility surface: Should Variant Inspector be a modal or a dedicated route? Modal is faster for quick operations; route may be better for deep investigation and bookmarks.
- Auto-fallback confidence thresholds: how to represent confidence and whether to allow auto-apply for enterprise tenants (opt-in).
- Sample storage and PII: how long to keep sampled requests/outputs, redaction rules, and policy for customer-sensitive data.
- UX for multi-variant rollbacks: if an experiment has 3 variants, how to visualize sequential vs simultaneous fallbacks and avoid accidental full experiment deletion.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Operator can open Variant Inspector from rollout detail and see metric cards and 3 sample outputs.
- Operator can execute "Reduce traffic" and "Fallback to baseline" actions with required comment and see the action recorded in timeline.
- System displays recommended action and shows expected impact (simple token/latency estimate).
- RBAC prevents non-authorized users from executing rollback/fallback.

Low-fidelity mock notes (for design handoff):
- Use compact row height for variant list to allow dense comparison (aim 6–8 variants visible without scroll).
- Metric cards should be colorblind-safe; use both icon + color.
- Decision panel should show "Why we recommend this" in one line; clicking expands the rule definition.
- Provide keyboard shortcuts: "i" to open inspector when a variant row is focused; "f" to trigger fallback confirmation flow.

Testing / evaluation plan:
- Internal canary: run on a non-production org with staged 5% traffic for 2 weeks. Capture false-positive/neg rates for auto recommendations.
- Usability study: 5 SRE/product engineers run through triage scenarios; record time-to-decision and confusion points.
- Metrics: mean-time-to-intervention, percent of interventions that were later reverted, and signals that led to correct decisions.

Next steps (immediate):
- Share with UX + SRE for quick 30-minute walkthrough (target: this Friday).
- Break down grooming tickets above and estimate (2-week sprint for MVP).
- Confluence writeup linking to design comps and sample outputs (see linked_artifacts).

Notes to self:
- Keep the first iteration conservative: require operator confirmation for any irreversible action.
- Make audit trail immutable and exportable for compliance customers.

Unresolved items to capture in tickets:
- Exact threshold defaults (p99 2s, quality-delta 5%) are suggestions and must be validated with historical data.
- Localization of microcopy and legal review for sampled data retention.

-- End of draft --

UX sketch filenames to attach in PR: variant-inspector-v1.png, inspector-decision-panel-rows.png
